outcome: A July 2025 preprint by Anup B. Dixit and Sushant Kala, 'A p-adic criterion for Lehmer's conjecture' (arXiv:2507.20141), proves Lehmer's conjecture for the restricted class of algebraic numbers α (of degree d, not a root of unity) having ≳ √(d log d) conjugates lying in a fixed finite extension of a p-adic field ℚ_p, via a p-adic equidistribution argument; the paper has since appeared in the International Journal of Number Theory (reported publication May 2026), which counts as expert digestion via peer review. The general conjecture remains open. No AI involvement was found in this or any other result located in the window.
summary: The decisive event in the window is Dixit and Kala's arXiv:2507.20141 (submitted 26 July 2025), which gives a p-adic criterion sufficient for Lehmer's conjecture: writing S_K(α) for the set of conjugates of α lying in a finite extension K of ℚ_p, the paper's Proposition 1.3 shows h(α) ≥ c/d (and hence Lehmer's conjecture) holds whenever |S_K(α)| ≳ √(d log d), with an explicit constant depending on q=|residue field| and [K:ℚ_p] (Corollary 1.4 gives the concrete threshold √(q³[K:ℚ_p] d log d)). This is a genuine case of the stated problem — it restricts the general question (all non-cyclotomic algebraic numbers) to a class defined by a p-adic clustering condition on conjugates, and proves the height bound for that class — so it is scoped correctly as `partial` per §3.1, not a variant. A web search snippet (via researcher.life/WorldScientific listings, which themselves 403'd on direct fetch) reports the paper has been formally published in the International Journal of Number Theory (May 2026); I could not independently load the WorldScientific page to confirm the DOI directly, so I treat this as likely but not fully verified — see confidence note below. Reading the full HTML version of the arXiv paper, the sole acknowledgement is INSPIRE Faculty Fellowship funding for the first author; there is no mention of any AI system, computational tool, or software anywhere in the paper, so ai_role is `none`. I also checked two other 2025 preprints that surface in searches for 'Lehmer's conjecture': arXiv:2506.18776 ('New evidence for Rémond's generalisation of Lehmer's conjecture') concerns heights on almost-split semiabelian varieties, a different algebraic-geometric analogue rather than the classical polynomial/Mahler-measure statement, and arXiv:2510.08871 ('Experimental investigations on Lehmer's conjecture for elliptic curves') concerns an analogous conjecture about canonical heights of non-torsion points on elliptic curves, again a distinct namesake conjecture, not the classical one about non-cyclotomic algebraic numbers' Mahler measure. Both are `related problems` under §3.1 and are excluded from the record. I also found and rejected a ResearchGate item, 'Lehmer's Conjecture as Computational Necessity: A Three-Pillar Synthesis of Information Theory, Arithmetic Fluid Dynamics, and Operational Geometry,' whose abstract (recovered via search snippet only, since the ResearchGate page itself returned HTTP 403) uses pseudo-technical invented terminology ('Irreducible Overhead Theorem', 'Arithmetic Fluid Dynamics', 'Ω_p attractor hierarchy') to claim the conjecture is a 'structural impossibility'; this reads as non-mathematical, likely AI-generated crank content rather than a real result, has no evident authorship or peer review, and I did not count it as an event of any kind — it is noted here only because it surfaced repeatedly in search and could otherwise be mistaken for a finding. The 2019 preprint claiming a full proof (arXiv:1911.10590) predates the window and, per the triage note and independent secondary reports, contains a fatal error, so it is not counted even as open_stale (it was never accepted as a resolution before or after the frozen date).
competing_reading: One could argue the Dixit-Kala result, while a genuine restriction of the domain, is narrow enough (a p-adic clustering condition satisfied by an unclear, possibly small, subset of algebraic numbers in practice) that it barely moves the needle on the conjecture as usually understood (Mahler measure bounded away from 1 for all non-cyclotomic algebraic integers). Under a stricter reading of 'case of the problem,' one might downgrade this to `progress` (a technique/bound) rather than `partial` (a settled case). I classify it as `partial` because the theorem does settle Lehmer's conjecture outright for a well-defined, non-empty class of algebraic numbers, which is exactly the pattern of the worked example in the instructions.
what_would_settle_it: Direct access to the WorldScientific/International Journal of Number Theory page (currently blocked by a 403 to automated fetchers) or another citation database (MathSciNet, zbMATH) confirming the DOI, volume, and publication date of the Dixit-Kala paper would fully confirm the peer-reviewed digestion and let `resolved`-level sourcing stand on firmer footing for that sub-claim (though the overall problem status of `partial` would not change, since the general conjecture is still open either way).
